spans.title: The Marble Lily
spans.blurb: A friend drops an Easter lily into a basin of strange liquid. What he lifts out is flawless marble, veined faintly blue, with a flush deep in its heart.

spans.title: Abandon All Hope
spans.blurb: Two travelers pass beneath a portal carved with terrible words, into starless air loud with sighs, and one asks his guide who these wailing souls are.

spans.title: Paolo and Francesca
spans.blurb: A ceaseless black wind whirls spirits like flocks of starlings. Two who fly together, light upon the storm, descend to tell how love brought them here.

books.pairNote: Two separate visions from different circles of the same journey; neither contains the other's payoff.

spans.title: The Secret Drawer
spans.blurb: Left alone with their mistress's jewels, a maid and her sweetheart press a hidden knob, and what springs out is worth more to her than any diamond.
spans.spoilerNote: Shows that the lady of the house secretly keeps a baby's shoe and lock of hair, an early planted clue to her hidden past.

spans.title: Danusia's Knight
spans.blurb: When a bench tips and a little singer totters, a young squire springs like a wildcat to catch her, and a laughing princess names him her knight.

spans.title: The Officer's Toast
spans.blurb: A drunken officer rises, glass in hand, to toast the prettiest girl in the room and take the rose beside her plate. Her look alone answers him.

spans.title: The Duel in the Clearing
spans.blurb: In a flowered clearing outside town, two young men face each other with pistols, while a terrified old second hides behind a bush to shout the count.

books.pairNote: The toast is the insult that provokes the duel, but each scene keeps its own payoff.

spans.title: The Face at the Window
spans.blurb: Reading after dinner, a man glances up to see eyes and ears above the window ledge. He takes it for a pig. It is no pig.

spans.title: The Creatures from the Pit
spans.blurb: A crash from the Pit sends dust boiling into the evening sky. A man takes his gun to the edge and looks down at what is climbing out.

books.pairNote: Both feature the same swine creatures, a first sighting and a later attack, but each scene has its own payoff.

spans.title: The Stranger on the Bridge
spans.blurb: Two proud men meet midway on a log bridge over a pebbly stream, and neither will give way. Staves are cut, and the question must be settled.

spans.title: The Impossible Mice
spans.blurb: She has heard squeals in the walls and means to write to the landlord. Then, out of the wainscoting, comes a single file of mice in colors mice never wear.

spans.title: The Runaway Elevator
spans.blurb: A maid mistakes a young man's camera case for a doctor's bag and runs him home to her mistress. The ornate house elevator has plans of its own.

books.pairNote: Separate comic episodes with different characters and different payoffs.

spans.title: New Year on the Auction Block
spans.blurb: While others keep holiday, a mother sits on a cold cabin floor, watching children who may be taken from her by morning. A witness sets down what she saw.

spans.title: A Letter from New York
spans.blurb: From a cramped hiding place, a runaway writes a letter for a trusted sailor to post far away, then waits, silent behind a door, to hear her hunter read it.

spans.title: The Buffoon and the Countryman
spans.blurb: A clown brings the theatre down with his imitation of a pig's squeal. A countryman swears he can do better, and hides something under his smock.
spans.brokenNote: The text ends mid-sentence on a comma, cutting off the countryman's closing retort that is the fable's point.

spans.title: A Handful of Fables
spans.blurb: A flattered crow, a wolf hunting for an excuse, a blind woman with a clever defense, and a god testing an honest woodman. Small tales with sharp points.

books.pairNote: Different fables entirely, with no shared text.
